newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS SAY READY TO BEGIN DIFFICULT TALKS WITH EU.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS SAY READY TO BEGIN DIFFICULT TALKS WITH EU.

text.p: The Czech Republic said it was ready to begin "difficult" negotiations after it was selected by the European Commission on Tuesday as one of six new states to begin accession talks to join the European Union.
"We know our qualities and we have discussed this with the European Union for a long time so this (decision) is the result," Foreign Ministry spokesman Vit Kurfuerst told Reuters.
"The negotiations will be difficult. We all remember the negotiation process of the last group of Scandinavian countries and Austria. So we expect a difficult process but we expect good results."
The European Commission formally agreed on Tuesday to recommend six nations for a first wave of EU entry talks, a Commission spokesman said.
He said the Commission's Agenda 2000 document was approved which recommends that Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia join Cyprus in the talks next year.
The document, obtained by Reuters ahead of the decision, tells East European applicants that they have to make more economic efforts before they enter the EU.
The document is to be formally present to the European parliament in Strasbourg on Wednesday.

Kurfuerst said that the Czech government still had much to do to standardise its laws and regulations with the Union, but that a commission for European integration led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus had been actively working on these tasks.
"We have a lot of tasks ahead and we are working on it," the ministry spokesman said.
The Czechs had originally hoped to be accepted into the EU by the turn of the century.

But structural problems within the EU and a lack of agreement among member states at the recent Amsterdam summit on how to change voting procedures in order to expand the Union, have many analysts saying the expansion will take place in the middle to end of the next decade.
